chunks: And with this chain, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), from his father (peace be upon him), from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever the Sublime God has bestowed a blessing upon, let him praise God the Sublime. And whoever finds his sustenance delayed, let him seek forgiveness from God. And whoever is saddened by a matter, let him say: There is no power nor any strength save by God.

key_terms.لا حَوْلَ وَلا قُوَّةَ إِلاّ بِاللَّهِ: There is no power nor strength save by God

ai.seo_question: What should one say when facing sorrow or delayed sustenance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the Imams from the Prophet, establishes a triad of spiritual responses to life's circumstances: gratitude (shukr) for blessings, repentance (istighfar) for delayed sustenance, and reliance (tawakkul) via the dhikr 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' for distress. In Shia tradition, this specific dhikr is revered as a key to Paradise and a means of accessing divine strength when human capacity is exhausted, linking human agency directly to God's will.
